title: Plumbing
summary: Learn practical plumbing: how water supply and pressure work, pipes, fittings and tools, storage tanks, rainwater harvesting and hot water, drainage and sanitation, common repairs and leak costs, and good practice and careers. Calculations were checked in code.
audience: Apprentices, homeowners, caretakers and anyone starting in the plumbing trade

body.p: Plumbing brings clean water into buildings, delivers it to taps and appliances, heats it, and carries wastewater safely away. Good plumbing is one of the greatest protections for public health: it prevents diseases such as cholera and typhoid.

list: The municipal main supplies water under pressure through a service pipe and a meter.
A stopcock (isolating valve) lets you shut off the supply to the whole building; everyone should know where it is.
Some buildings feed taps directly from the main; others fill a storage tank, often on a stand or roof, that supplies taps by gravity.
Backflow preventers and air gaps stop dirty water being drawn back into the supply.

body.p: Water pressure from a tank depends on its height above the outlet (the head). Pressure = ρgh: a tank 10 m above a tap gives about 1000 x 9.81 x 10 = 98 100 Pa, about 98 kPa or roughly 1 bar. Low tanks give weak showers; very high mains pressure may need a pressure-reducing valve to protect fittings.

body.tip: Label the main stopcock and test that it turns; in an emergency every second counts.

list: PVC and uPVC: used for cold water and drainage; joined with solvent cement.
Polyethylene (HDPE): flexible pipe for supply and irrigation, joined with compression fittings or fusion welding.
PEX and multilayer pipe: flexible pipe for hot and cold water inside buildings.
Copper: durable for hot and cold water, joined by soldering or compression fittings.
Galvanised steel: found in older buildings; corrodes over time, reducing flow.

body.p: Elbows change direction, tees create branches, reducers change pipe size, unions allow parts to be disconnected, and valves (gate, ball, non-return) control flow. Thread tape or paste seals threaded joints.

Common tools include pipe wrenches, adjustable spanners, a hacksaw or pipe cutter, deburring tool, tape measure, spirit level, blowtorch for copper, and a pressure-test pump. Cutting pipe squarely and removing burrs makes joints that do not leak.

body.tip: Use the right pipe for the job: PVC pressure pipe for supply is different from thinner drainage pipe.

body.p: A tank 2 m x 1 m x 1 m holds 2 m³, or 2000 litres. If five people each use about 50 litres a day, that is 250 litres a day, so a full tank lasts 2000 / 250 = 8 days without refilling. Tanks should be covered, cleaned regularly and placed on a strong, level base: water weighs 1 kg per litre, so 2000 litres weighs about 2 tonnes.

A roof of 8 m x 5 m in an area with 150 mm of rain in a month collects about 8 x 5 x 0.15 = 6 m³ of rain; allowing for 80% efficiency (losses from splashing and first flush), that is 4800 litres, enough for that household for about 19 days.

list: Electric geysers (storage water heaters) heat water with an element controlled by a thermostat.
Every geyser must have a pressure-relief valve and a drain pipe; a faulty or blocked valve can cause a dangerous burst.
Solar water heaters greatly reduce electricity use.
Insulating hot pipes and setting the thermostat to around 55 to 60 °C saves energy while limiting bacteria such as Legionella.

body.tip: Install a geyser timer to heat water only when needed.

body.p: Drainage carries wastewater by gravity, so pipes must slope (fall) in the right direction.

list: A fall of 1 in 40 drops 25 mm for every metre: a 6 m run falls 150 mm.
Too little fall lets solids settle and block; very steep falls can leave solids behind as water rushes ahead.
Traps (U-bends) under sinks, basins and toilets hold water that blocks sewer gases from entering the building.
Vent pipes let air into the system so traps are not sucked dry.
Inspection eyes and manholes allow blockages to be cleared.

body.p: Where there is no sewer, options include septic tanks with soakaways, ventilated improved pit (VIP) latrines and urine-diverting dry toilets. They must be sited away from boreholes and wells, often at least about 15 to 30 m depending on soil and local rules, to protect groundwater.

body.tip: Never pour fats and cooking oil down drains; they set and cause blockages.

body.p: Leaks waste water and money. A tap leaking 0.1 litres a minute loses 0.1 x 1440 = 144 litres a day, or 4320 litres a month. At a tariff of R0.03 per litre (R30 per kilolitre), that is about R129.60 a month.

list: Dripping taps: replace the washer or cartridge.
Running toilets: adjust or replace the float valve or flush valve.
Check for hidden leaks by reading the meter when no water is being used; if it moves, there is a leak.
Blocked drains: use a plunger or drain rod; avoid harsh chemicals that damage pipes.
Low pressure: check for closed valves, blocked filters or corroded pipes.
Burst pipes: shut the stopcock first, then repair with the right coupling.

body.tip: Keep spare washers, thread tape and a plunger in the house; most small repairs need nothing more.

list: Pressure-test new pipework before covering it, and check for leaks over time.
Support pipes at regular intervals with clips and brackets.
Protect pipes from frost in cold areas and from sunlight (UV) where plastic pipes are exposed.
Install isolation valves on each fixture so repairs do not cut water to the whole building.
Follow national plumbing regulations and get compliance certificates where required.

body.p: Low-flow showerheads, dual-flush toilets, tap aerators and fixing leaks quickly reduce demand, which matters in water-stressed cities. Greywater from basins and showers can be reused for gardens with simple systems.

Plumbers train through apprenticeships, technical colleges and trade tests. Work includes new buildings, maintenance, irrigation, solar water heating and running a small business. Reliability and clean, tidy work build a strong reputation.

body.tip: Photograph pipe routes before walls are closed; it helps future repairs.
